resources.string: MindHeed detects when you keep scrolling in Instagram and gradually veils the screen, then offers a bubble that takes you back to your saved posts. It only knows which app is open and that a scroll happened. It cannot read anything on your screen, and nothing leaves your phone.

MindHeed uses Android’s Accessibility service to work on top of Instagram.

What it uses:
• which app is in front (to know when Instagram is open)
• the fact that a scroll happened in Instagram (to count how many posts you scroll past)

What it does with it: shows a gradual veil over Instagram and a bubble that opens your saved posts.

What it never does: read your screen, your messages or your passwords. It collects nothing and sends nothing: everything stays on your phone. It only downloads, from time to time, a small public settings file (thresholds, latest version).

On the next screen, select MindHeed, then turn it on.

The first posts you scroll past stay clear. Then, post after post, the screen veils over. When it gets strong, a bubble appears: tap it to open your saved posts. They open with no veil and no limit while you stay in Instagram, and the counter starts over. Only the main feed is counted.

Test: scroll exactly 10 posts in Instagram, then come back here. The number closest to 10 tells which counter matches the posts best.
The system may stop MindHeed in the background. In Settings › Apps › MindHeed: turn on Autostart and set Battery saver to “No restrictions”.

MindHeed collects no personal data.

• The Accessibility service only receives the name of the app in front and a “scroll happened” signal from Instagram. It cannot read screen content.
• Your settings and your Instagram username are stored only on your phone.
• MindHeed has no account, no analytics and no ads. It only reads a public settings file, without sending anything about you.
• Uninstalling the app deletes everything.

MindHeed is not affiliated with Instagram or Meta.
